note: Item text transcribed from the official IMO 2015 English problem paper. Code derivation is core-model pattern 1: data/imos_2018.r does select(starts_with('Problem')) then pivot_longer(names_to='item'), so the IRW item code IS the source CSV's own column name (case-folded to lowercase) -- no positional assignment anywhere in the chain. The 2015 paper prints 'Problem 1'..'Problem 6' outright across its two day pages (Day 1 = Problems 1-3, Friday 10 July; Day 2 = Problems 4-6, Saturday 11 July), so the numbering is read directly and no day convention had to be inferred. Deviations disclosed: typeset mathematics rendered in plain-text ASCII -- calligraphic S written 'S', blackboard-bold R written 'R', Greek capitals written 'Gamma'/'Omega', script ell written 'l', the relation symbols written '>=', '<=', '!=', the function arrow written '->', superscripts with '^' (2^n, 1007^2), subscripts with '_' (a_1, a_2, a_j, a_k, a_l), the angle sign written 'angle' and the degree sign '90 degrees', and the summation written inline as |sum_(j=m+1)^n (a_j - b)| -- the absolute-value bars are printed in the source and pdftotext drops them, so they were read off a 150dpi page render (the plain-text stream shows a bare '(aj - b) <= 10072', which is that same flattening plus the lost superscript; anyone re-extracting from text alone should not read either as a discrepancy). This whole PDF's text layer is encoded with a mangled custom glyph mapping (pdftotext returns dingbats: 'Pr#b#em' style output), so the entire transcription was made against 150dpi page renders of both pages rather than the extracted text. Problem 1's (a)/(b) parts, Problem 2's displayed line 'ab - c, bc - a, ca - b', Problem 5's displayed functional equation, and Problem 6's (i)/(ii) conditions and displayed sum are inlined into the running sentence rather than kept as display lines. Wording otherwise verbatim, including 'centre-free', 'orthocentre', 'circumcentre' and the paper's own '. . .' ellipsis. instructions holds the footer printed identically at the foot of both day pages ('Time: 4 hours and 30 minutes' / 'Each problem is worth 7 points'), which is whole-table framing; the per-day language/day/date headers are section_prompt only. option_text is blank (NA) on all 48 rows and correct_response on all 48: resp 0-7 is a jury mark out of 7 for a written proof, so there is nothing to select and no scoring key, and the unlabelled mark points were deliberately not padded with their own numbers. Rights: fetched https://www.imo-official.org/problems.aspx on 2026-09-07 -- 'licen', 'commercial', 'redistribut' and 'permission' appear nowhere on the page, the only 'copyright' hit is the bare footer '(c) International Mathematical Olympiad', and the PDF carries no notice; nothing quotable, so silence-is-permission applies (same finding as the batch_049/050/051/052 imos_* tables).
public_note: The IMO problem paper is sat by each contestant in their own language; the item text shipped here is the organisers' official English version, so it is the canonical instrument rather than the wording any particular contestant read.

source_ref: Wright A & Diamond A (2014) 'An effect of inhibitory load in children while keeping working memory load constant', Front. Psychol. 5:213, doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2014.00213 (CC BY, PMC3954128); item/resp semantics from data/imps2025_hf.R; administration details from Obradovic, Sulik, Finch & Tirado-Strayer (2018) doi:10.1016/j.appdev.2017.03.003 and DeJoseph et al. note: Hearts and Flowers task (Davidson et al. 2006), a picture-stimulus task: the stimulus is a red heart or a red flower and there is no item wording, so item_text is blank by design under the 2026-09-05 picture-stimulus ruling. The item code is not inferred: data/imps2025_hf.R keeps the raw stim_shape and stim_side fields and `item` is their concatenation, which a server-side GROUP BY over the live table confirms in all 8 item x stim_shape x stim_side cells with 0 exceptions (114,823 rows). option_text labels the accuracy coding the same script defines (heart: correct iff resp_side==stim_side; flower: correct iff resp_side!=stim_side), verified against the live data with 0 violating rows; correct_response is left blank because resp is already an accuracy score rather than a response choice. Both of the study's own papers are closed access (OpenAlex oa_status=closed for both DOIs, checked 2026-09-07) and the same project's open description of this exact administration (Finch, Garcia, Sulik & Obradovic 2019, AERA Open, doi:10.1177/2332858419829438) is CC BY-NC, so no wording was copied from it; instructions and the two rule prompts are transcribed verbatim from the CC BY Wright & Diamond (2014) description of the standard task instead. The Finch (2019) description was read only to confirm the administration matches (12 congruent / 12 incongruent / 33 mixed trials, 750 ms response window raised to 1,250 ms in spring), which it does exactly, including the 750/1250 split hard-coded in data/imps2025_hf.R. No fee or redistribution clause is quotable for this paradigm; the wording shipped comes from a CC BY article.
public_note: Item text for this table is blank by design: Hearts and Flowers stimuli are pictures (a red heart or a red flower) with no wording, and the item code names the stimulus and the side it appeared on. The instructions shipped are the canonical description of the standard task rather than this study's own script, which was never published; this study administered it to groups of children on tablets with side-mounted response buttons and a 750 ms (spring: 1,250 ms) response deadline, where the canonical description is of an individually administered touchscreen version.

note: The deposit's codebook.txt keys each item code to its wording ("AS1 Express myself easily.") and data/ipip_openpsychometrics.r takes item straight from the source column names (select(starts_with("AS")) then pivot_longer(names_to="item")), so the IRW codes AS1-AS10 ARE the data.csv header names -- no positional step, nothing inferred. ORCHESTRATOR RECONCILIATION (batch_053 close): as first written this table shipped the codebook's bare stems ("Express myself easily.") with the prefix sentence carried in instructions, while the sibling ipip_openpsychometrics_do -- same deposit, same codebook.txt -- applied the prefix. The orchestrator re-read the codebook, which states outright "All were prefixed with \"I \"." on its own line above the item listing, so the prefixed form is the ADMINISTERED wording and the bare stem is only the codebook's listing convention. item_text was rewritten to the prefixed form with the stem's first word lowercased, matching the sibling exactly; instructions still carries the codebook sentence. Both agents independently transcribed the same anchors including the source typo "Neither agree not disagree" (sic), which corroborates the anchor row.
public_note: The codebook lists the IPIP stems without their leading pronoun and notes that all items were administered prefixed with "I "; the shipped item_text applies that prefix ("I express myself easily.").
